answer: One concrete defence is a delta check on verified work: before an agent can earn, it must stake a deposit and complete a costly, identity-bound computation that peers verify, so the change between a real identity and a fake one is measurable, not just claimed. A mirror of cheap copies then fails, because each copy must pay the full stake and computation separately, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its proof. Like jade that must be cut and tested before it is trusted, identity is earned through a cost that cannot be copied for free.
